name: Dorsal approach to multiple metatarsals
corridor: Dorsal longitudinal incisions in the intermetatarsal grooves (between 1st-2nd and/or 3rd-4th) with adequate skin bridges, working between the long and short extensor tendons to reach several metatarsals

positioning.text: Position supine with the foot at the end of the table under tourniquet control.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the intermetatarsal grooves and the long and short extensor tendons of each involved ray.

incision.text: Use one incision between the 1st and 2nd and, or, one between the 3rd and 4th metatarsals, avoiding more than two close parallel incisions to preserve skin vitality.

superficial_interval.text: Preserve the longitudinal dorsal veins and identify and protect the branches of the deep peroneal nerve that provide superficial digital innervation.

deep_interval.text: Enter between the long and short extensor tendons of the corresponding ray without cutting muscle, releasing muscle from bone and elevating periosteum to reach each metatarsal.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with dorsal veins and intermetatarsal nerves, the long and short extensor tendons, and the metatarsals.

structures_at_risk.text: The intermetatarsal branches of the deep peroneal nerve and the crossing superficial veins are at risk, and the skin bridges are at risk of necrosis if incisions are too close.

danger_zones.text: Narrow skin bridges between parallel incisions are the danger zone for skin necrosis.

retraction_hazards.text: Preserve longitudinal veins and intermetatarsal nerves and avoid undermining the skin bridges.

exposure.text: Exposes multiple metatarsal shafts through the intermetatarsal windows.

limitations.text: No more than two parallel incisions can be used safely, limiting how many adjacent metatarsals are exposed at once.

indications.text: Indicated for fixation of multiple metatarsal fractures.

closure.text: Close any joint capsule with resorbable sutures, repair the tendon sheath where possible, and close subcuticular tissue with resorbable sutures and skin with nylon.

complications.text: Complications include skin bridge necrosis, dorsal cutaneous nerve injury, and extensor tendon adhesions.

procedure_applications.condition: Several metatarsal fractures require simultaneous dorsal exposure

questions.question: Where are the incisions placed for multiple metatarsal exposure?
questions.answer: Between the 1st and 2nd and/or the 3rd and 4th metatarsals.

questions.question: Why should more than two close parallel incisions be avoided?
questions.answer: They compromise the vitality of the skin bridges.

questions.question: Which nerve branches must be protected dorsally?
questions.answer: The branches of the deep peroneal nerve providing superficial digital innervation.
